Charged Cartan Monte Carlo — Experiment 04: Σ_AB Choi-state Q-conservation¶

Status: complete Tracks: GitHub issue #16, PR #21 (merged) Milestone: Charged Cartan Monte Carlo v0.2 Result: eliminates the discrete Q-drift bug from Experiment 03 (finite-size) while preserving the headline plateau within 0.1.

TL;DR¶

A Choi-state representation of Σ_AB (design note v0.2 § Σ_AB-dimension mismatch) fixes the discrete Q-drift bug surfaced by Experiment 03 § Discrete Q-drift. The fix is on by default since the merge of #16. Headline geometry (peak D_S ≈ 4.6 plateau) is preserved within 0.1; Q drift drops from integer ±1–20 (in ~60–70% of seeds) to floating-point noise ~10⁻⁵ in ~22% of seeds. CP-violation still produces structural drift at γ_CP > 0 — the fix doesn’t mask real physics.

Context¶

Experiment 03 ran a finite-size investigation of the v0.2 plateau and incidentally surfaced a structural bug: at γ_CP = 0 (where Q should be exactly conserved), 95 of 160 runs (59%) showed integer Q drift across the tune. The mechanism was traced to the v0.2 first pass storing the bowtie’s joint state rhoAB redundantly as (xp, ab) and (ab, yp) entries in quditJointOf_, while the single-vertex proxy quditStateOf_[ab] = I/4 was inconsistent with both joints. When ab was later consumed as input to a new interaction, the joint took over and “discovered” the proxy-hidden charge as frontier drift.

The principled fix, designed in the v0.2 design note’s Σ_AB-as-Choi-state section: replace the I/4 proxy with the full Choi state J(U) = (U ⊗ I)|Ω⟩⟨Ω|(U† ⊗ I) of the interaction unitary, and store the cross-products correlation (xp, yp) once rather than duplicating it across (xp, ab) and (ab, yp).

Hypothesis¶

If the Choi-state representation is structurally correct, three things should hold simultaneously:

  1. Q is exactly conserved under interact at γ_CP = 0 (the bug is fixed).

  2. The v0.2 plateau (peak D_S ≈ 4.6) is preserved — the fix only changes Q-bookkeeping, not the geometry the action selects.

  3. CP-violation still drifts Q at γ_CP > 0 — the fix mustn’t mask real CP-violating physics.

Reproduce¶

The sanity-scan plot and plotter live on the GitHub releases page as issue-attachments assets (not in the repo tree). To regenerate locally:

# Run the scan via the worker (saved under /tmp during development)
OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2 \
MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 BLIS_NUM_THREADS=2 \
python /tmp/choi_sanity_scan.py

C++ regression: ctest -R test_sigma_ab_choi_state (in build-quantum/). 22/22 tests across all interaction suites pass.

CP-violation preservation¶

In the C++ test suite (test_sigma_ab_choi_state.cpp), at γ_CP = 0.5 the Q drift over 50 cells is −1.31 with Choi on. The structural CP-violation effect is not masked by the bookkeeping fix.

Findings¶

  1. The bug is fixed. Discrete integer Q drift becomes float-precision round-off. The Choi flag is on by default after PR #21, so all post-#21 v0.2 runs get the fix automatically.

  2. The plateau is preserved. The headline 4.6 ≈ D_S finding from Experiment 02 is robust to this representational change. Per-β means agree within 0.1 across the plateau region.

  3. Surprise: the principled “Choi state” is mostly a justification for the actual fix, which was the structural change to joint storage. The 256-dim Choi state’s marginal on a single ququart is in fact I/4 (the maximally-mixed state) — exactly what the v0.2 first pass was using as a proxy. The reason the proxy was wrong wasn’t because it disagreed with what Choi would predict; it was because the v0.2 first pass duplicated the joint rhoAB as both (xp, ab) and (ab, yp) in the joint storage, and the duplicated joints overcounted ab’s effective charge content. The Choi framing forced us to notice the duplication and store the joint once as (xp, yp).

Limitations / open questions¶

  • The plateau-value uncertainty (4.6 ± 0.1 vs the target 4) is unaffected by this fix — the Choi representation is about Q-bookkeeping, not geometry. Closing the 0.6 offset is still on the table for Experiment 05 (T = 100k deep scan) and the Hamiltonian-parameter scan (issue #11).

  • The Choi state is computationally cheap (built once, 256×256 pure-state matrix, ~kB memory), so there’s no performance cost to having it on by default.
